Hiring Team\\
Nile Robotics\\
Re: Senior Machine Learning Engineer \textendash{} Data Systems
tokens.BODY_BLOCKS:
I am writing about the Senior Machine Learning Engineer role. For four years I have built inference systems that stay up \textemdash{} the kind of work your posting describes \textperiodcentered{} at the scale it describes it.

At Nile Robotics I cut inference latency 38\% across twelve services and held p99 under 80\,ms. The pipeline behind that number processes \textit{4\,TB a day}, and the \textbf{reinforcement-learning} component that schedules it is the piece I would bring here first. The write-up is at \href{https://example.com/report}{example.com/report}.

Two details from the posting stood out. The first is ownership of the serving path end to end \textendash{} something I have done rather than supervised. The second is the emphasis on measurement: every claim above is a figure I can decompose on request, and I would rather show the derivation than the headline.

Before that I automated ingestion for thirty-odd sources as a data engineering intern at NiaDelta, which is where I learned how much of reliability is really about the boring parts \textbar{} naming, retries, and the willingness to delete a clever thing. Ligatures: efficient offices affix fluffy waffles.

One project shipped under a budget of \$40\,000 with a 95\% uptime target; the config lived in \{scheduler\}, the metric was named p99\_latency, and the on-call rota was \#serving. Approximate cost per request fell by a factor of \textasciitilde{}3, error rate by 2\textasciicircum{}-4, and the escape hatch was a literal \textbackslash{} in the template that used to break the build. R\&D signed off in June.

I would welcome a conversation about where the team needs the most help, and I am happy to walk through any of the above in detail.
